text: Problem 4: the adversarial reader returned (read-only, served c5c10_sparring_brief.md and the source passages; its reasons quoted in the finding). Its hardest reasons: against (a), the composition test and an uneven use of Grasse, since the page that excludes proposals also excludes relations between workers, and Moffett et al.'s Venice case puts hub-like explicit signaling on the far side of stigmergy (p. 64: the response 'moved ... from stigmergy and swarming to explicit signaling'); against (c), the rule written before the tally; against (d), losing the difference in functioning and having to pick one universal problem. Checked: Grasse 1959, p. 75, 'Plus n'est besoin de faire appel a des relations entre individus, ni a un plan suivi par les Termites', and then 'la prudence conseille de ne pas eliminer toute possibilite d'une cooperation ou d'une information entre ouvriers'; the 237 rooms of T3-038 and of T4-008's members are both correct (counted), a coincidence. An option named before it is weighed: (e) keep the theme, its one member and its place in D02 (information provision), and name it for what its records show in Okhuysen and Bechky's terms, 'Direct information sharing' (2009, p. 474: representations give 'a common space' where groups 'post information that is vital for the current task'; 'posting information also makes the activities of the different groups visible, which helps coordinate their future work'), with stigmergy told apart in its mistaken_for.

Problem 4, the decision, weighed under the four rules logged first. (a) keep Stigmergy, one member: records yes (10 of 14 bearing records report the work's state); organization-design source weak (Moffett et al. 2021 admit stigmergy in temporary organizing but describe a move 'from stigmergy and swarming to explicit signaling', p. 64; stigmergy needs no 'relations entre individus', Grasse 1959, p. 75, and the records are members' posts); D02 whole, but no grouping; claims the placing the record does not hold. (b) withdraw: no D02 theme takes T3-038, and it would erase a difference in functioning (F-022). (c) return T3-041 and T3-060: overrides the rule written before the tally. (d) merge with Standardization of output: groups six members and Okhuysen and Bechky admit it, but it joins two routes the rooms carry apart (89 both, independence 80; F-022) and two universal problems (information, division), and two of T4-008's members are not objects. (e) keep the theme, its member, its place and its mapping, renamed Direct information sharing (Okhuysen and Bechky 2009, p. 474): records yes; source yes; D02 whole, no grouping (stated with its reason); theory question served (posting the work's state is a route of its own, apart from task division); claims nothing beyond the record. Chosen: (e), on rules 2 and 4 and the tie-break; its cost, the one-member break of C2's criterion, is stated in the declaration. 'Aligned' restored in D02 with its count (F-021).

T4-007 Move (developing or dropping working hypotheses), problem 4, Stigmergy and 'aligned': 6 field(s) amended. The working hypothesis that this theme's records show stigmergy is dropped, and the theme is named for what they show: members post the state of the shared work in the thread. Weighed under the rule logged first (diary, C5c-10): option (e) keeps the member and the theme's place in D02 and in information provision (C3 mapping), is named by the organization-design source that admits its records (Okhuysen and Bechky 2009, p. 474), and claims nothing the record cannot show; Stigmergy claimed the placing that would answer the posts, which the record does not hold, and stigmergy needs no 'relations entre individus' (Grasse 1959, p. 75). Options (b), (c) and (d) fail as set out in finding-4; the adversarial reader's reasons are quoted there. Findings touched: F-018 bounded by a superseding line (the recut stands; the theme renamed); F-022 written.

D02 Move (developing or dropping working hypotheses), problem 4, Stigmergy and 'aligned': 3 field(s) amended. 'Aligned' restored with its count, under the rule logged first (diary, C5c-10): in 233 of the 370 rooms that called for hands, the room's record reports a work up after its first call (F-021, c5c10_aligned.py); Okhuysen and Bechky 2009 (p. 469) take 'a goal, task, or piece of work is achieved' as what definitions of coordination share. The predicate and the disconfirming clause take the renamed theme's words. Findings touched: F-021 written.

C5c-10 closing: problem 4 (Stigmergy and 'aligned') done. Finding: out/serial-C5/finding-4-stigmergy-aligned.md. Rules written first; options (d) and (e) named before weighing; Moffett et al. 2021, Okhuysen and Bechky 2009 and Grasse 1959 cited from the page; one adversarial reader, read-only, served a brief and no notes. Chosen (e): T4-007 keeps its one member, its place in D02 and its mapping to information provision, renamed Direct information sharing (move 168); D02 says the room aligned many hands, 233 of 370 rooms with calls reporting a work up after the first call (move 169); F-021, F-022 written; F-018 superseded (bounded); pass 13 (prefer). Ledgers: tier_history 561, findings 33, account_passes 13. Head 3,000 words, links resolve; validate.py C5: 0 errors, 0 warnings; no .pause. No slips noted beyond one: the spec first wrote Grasse without its accent, corrected before the write.

Problem 2 (the reason test), the rules written before any read. J's framing kept: omission against commission, and survivor bias weighed before the asymmetry is read. A. SURVIVAL, counted before any reply is read (no text shown): for every item carrying a cited concept of the calls element (P01) and every item carrying one of the attack element (P09) (c2_elements_c5c2.json themes, assignments_final support_by_theme), the direct replies by another author (items.jsonl, parent_id), by state: coded (its text survives in the coded record and can be read), bridge (uncoded, kept for a coded descendant), collapsed (uncoded, no text in the record); and with author [deleted]. Reported by kind of call. F-014 drew only coded replies, so the share of direct replies that went uncoded bounds what any reason test on this record can read. B. THE TEST ON CALLS TO PLACE: one pair per room; the first part is the earliest item in the room carrying a P01 concept that has a coded direct reply by another author; the reply is the earliest such coded direct reply, its coded passages joined in text order. 80 rooms drawn with random.Random(20261015) from the rooms with a pair. Read whole; a pair counts only if its first part, read whole, calls or invites members to place for a work (not an attack call; others set aside and counted). Codes as in c3b_ca_codes.json: stance accept (joins, assents, gives a location or tactic, reports doing it), refuse (declines, forbids, redirects away, says it cannot be done), mixed, other; account: a clause giving a reason or ground (a because, since or so clause, a stated rule or norm, a fact offered as a ground, a consequence); a bare assent, a bare refusal, a directive with no ground, an evaluation, a joke, a tactic or a report of action is not an account. Fisher's exact test, one-sided, refusals giving a reason more often than acceptances. Coded by me alone. C. WHAT IT CAN CHANGE: F-014's bound (a new finding for calls to place); A12's mechanism (the bare answer, theorised) if acceptances to calls to place come bare and refusals with a reason; the account reads the asymmetry as a fact about written, coded replies.

Problem 2, part A, survival (c5c11_survival.py; no reply text read). Calls to place (items carrying a P01 concept): 1,949; 920 (0.472) have a direct reply by another author in the record, 756 a coded one; of 2,858 direct replies, 2,258 are coded (0.790), 306 bridge, 283 collapsed, 11 removed; uncoded with author [deleted] 35 (0.012). Attack calls (P09 items): 1,565; 682 (0.436) have a direct reply, 520 a coded one; of 1,271 direct replies, 942 coded (0.741), 100 bridge, 227 collapsed, 2 removed; uncoded with author [deleted] 14 (0.011). Read as J frames it: more than half of all calls of either kind carry no written reply at all, so most answers, whatever they were, are not in the writing (omission against commission: placing leaves no line in the thread). Of the replies written, a fifth to a quarter carry no coded text and cannot be read, a little more under attack calls; deletion is about one reply in a hundred under either kind. So the record's filter is mostly what was never written or never coded, not what was later removed, and it is close to the same for both kinds of call. The stance of a reply that left no text cannot be known, so no reading here can say whether acceptances were written or coded less than refusals.

Problem 2, part B, read and tallied (c5c11_place_codes.json, c5c11_place_tally.py): 285 rooms have a call to place with a coded direct reply; 80 drawn (seed 20261015). 17 set aside (the first part a report, an acceptance or outreach to other subs). Of 63 kept: accept 31, refuse 3, mixed 2, other 27 (questions, reports, jokes, bot and moderator notices). Reasons: refusals 3 of 3, acceptances 6 of 31, mixed 2 of 2; one-sided Fisher p 0.014; 25 bare acceptances, median 9 words. Read with part A first: the stance ratio in writing (31 to 3) is not the room's, since most calls carry no written reply and an acceptance can be done by placing; refusing a call to place is mostly not written at all. Within the written, coded replies, the asymmetry F-014 found on attack calls holds on calls to place, on few refusals. In the contract's terms: a refusal is the room contesting what to act on, and it is said with a ground; an acceptance settles it, and is mostly done or said bare. Writes: F-023; F-014 superseded (bounded: the 38 against 14 set by the draw; the asymmetry is a fact about written, coded replies); A12's bound and mechanism next.
